meta.label: Vacuum cleaners
tradeoffLabels: owner can fix what wears out
meta.attribution: Compares 17 specific vacuum cleaners on sale in the UK: corded uprights and cylinders, cordless sticks and robot vacuums from Dyson, Shark, Miele, Numatic (Henry), Vax, Hoover, Bissell, Kärcher, Roborock, iRobot, Ecovacs and eufy. Price is what the maker's own UK shop, or John Lewis where the maker was not checked directly, listed on the day checked. It is scored as 100 minus one point per £10, between 5 and 95; sale prices move often, and the note gives the figure seen. Guarantee length is the guarantee stated on the same listing or the maker's own guarantee page: 1 year scores 30, 2 years 50, 3 years 65 and 5 years 85. That sits on top of UK consumer law, which lets a buyer claim for faults present at purchase for up to six years whatever the guarantee says. Repairability asks whether the owner can deal with the part that usually fails first. A corded machine, which has no battery to wear out, scores 70. A cordless machine whose listing says the battery can be removed or swapped also scores 70. A spare battery included in the box, or sold separately by the maker, adds 5 or 10. A corded machine whose maker publishes exploded parts diagrams scores 80. Where a listing does not say whether the battery can be removed, repairability is left blank rather than guessed. France's repairability index covers vacuum cleaners, but the files on data.gouv.fr cover only a few of these brands, so it is not used here. Privacy is scored only for the four robot vacuums, which map the home through an app. They start from 50. A national regulator's security finding against the brand lowers the score: Korea's Internet & Security Agency and Consumer Agency tested six robot vacuums in 2025 and found weaknesses in several Chinese-made models. Sending data outside the UK and EEA to countries with weaker protection lowers it a little. The stick, upright and cylinder machines here are not given a privacy score. iRobot was bought out of Chapter 11 by its contract manufacturer Picea in January 2026; its entry says so. Suction power and cleaning results are not scored, because no independent test covering all these models was read. Sources: maker UK shops and guarantee pages, John Lewis listings, iRobot's SEC filing, Korean regulator findings as reported by Korea JoongAng Daily and Asia Economy, eufy's privacy policy. Four of the seventeen are robot vacuums, although the map also has a separate robot-vacuums decision; they are compared here alongside the other machines rather than moved. Reviewed 2026-10. Suggest changes via Contribute.

criteria.label: Owner can replace what wears out

products.name: Dyson V15 Detect Absolute
products.description: Dyson's best-known cordless stick, with a laser-lit floor head and a dust sensor. The dearest stick here after Miele's Triflex.

economical.note: Dyson's UK shop listed it at £649.99 when checked. Scored as 100 minus one point per £10, so a £150 machine scores 85 and a £650 one 35.

longevity.note: John Lewis's listing for the Dyson V15 Detect Absolute states a 2-year guarantee.

repairability.note: John Lewis's listing describes an easily removable click-in battery that detaches and reattaches at the click of a button, so the part that wears out first on a cordless vacuum can be changed by the owner without tools.

products.name: Dyson V8 Cyclone
products.description: Dyson's cheaper current cordless stick, an updated V8 with a swappable battery and a claimed 60-minute run time in eco mode.

economical.note: Dyson's UK shop listed it at £349.99 when checked. Scored as 100 minus one point per £10, so a £150 machine scores 85 and a £650 one 35.

longevity.note: John Lewis's listing for the Dyson V8 Cyclone states a 2-year guarantee.

repairability.note: Dyson's UK product page and John Lewis's listing both describe a swappable 7-cell lithium battery, which the owner can change without sending the machine away.

products.name: Shark PowerDetect Speed cordless (IA1241UK)
products.description: A mid-priced Shark cordless stick. Its battery is listed but John Lewis does not say whether the owner can swap it, so repairability is not scored.

economical.note: John Lewis listed it at £419.99 when checked. Scored as 100 minus one point per £10, so a £150 machine scores 85 and a £650 one 35.

longevity.note: John Lewis's listing for model IA1241UK states a 2-year guarantee.

products.name: Shark LU251UK corded upright
products.description: A corded Shark upright with the longest guarantee in this list at five years.

economical.note: John Lewis listed it at £179.99 when checked. Scored as 100 minus one point per £10, so a £150 machine scores 85 and a £650 one 35.

longevity.note: John Lewis's listing for model LU251UK states a 5-year guarantee.

repairability.note: A corded upright, so there is no battery to wear out; John Lewis's listing notes a removable brush-roll and washable filters that the owner can clean or change.

products.name: Miele Guard M1 Flex bagged cylinder
products.description: A corded, bagged Miele cylinder vacuum, Miele's mainstream corded model.

economical.note: John Lewis listed it at £289.00 when checked. Scored as 100 minus one point per £10, so a £150 machine scores 85 and a £650 one 35.

longevity.note: John Lewis's listing for the Miele Guard M1 Flex states a 2-year guarantee.

repairability.note: A corded, bagged cylinder, so there is no battery to wear out; John Lewis's listing lists the hose, tube, floorhead, nozzles and filter as separate parts in the box.

products.name: Miele Triflex HX3 Plus cordless
products.description: Miele's premium cordless, the most expensive machine in this list, sold with two removable batteries.

economical.note: John Lewis listed it at £899.00 when checked. Scored as 100 minus one point per £10, so a £150 machine scores 85 and a £650 one 35.

longevity.note: John Lewis's listing for model 12878430 states a 2-year guarantee.

repairability.note: John Lewis's listing says the box includes a removable battery and an additional battery, so the owner can swap packs and has a spare from the start.

products.name: Henry Plus (Numatic)
products.description: The smiling red tub vacuum, built by Numatic in Chard, Somerset. Corded and bagged, with exploded parts diagrams published for repairers.

economical.note: John Lewis listed it at £189.99 when checked. Scored as 100 minus one point per £10, so a £150 machine scores 85 and a £650 one 35.

longevity.note: John Lewis's listing for the Henry Plus states a 2-year guarantee.

repairability.note: Henry is a corded, bagged cylinder, so there is no battery to wear out. Numatic, the Somerset firm that makes it, points owners to a dedicated support site for support, technical data and exploded diagrams, the parts maps an owner or local repairer needs.

products.name: Vax Blade 4 Pet cordless
products.description: A low-priced cordless stick from Vax, with a removable battery shared across its ONEPWR range.

economical.note: John Lewis listed it at £149.99 when checked. Scored as 100 minus one point per £10, so a £150 machine scores 85 and a £650 one 35.

longevity.note: John Lewis's listing for the Vax Blade 4 Pet states a 3-year guarantee.

repairability.note: Vax sells the ONEPWR battery and charger separately on its own site, priced at £99.00 for the kit when checked, and says the interchangeable battery fits all VAX ONEPWR products, which includes this Blade 4 Pet's removable 4.0Ah pack.

products.name: Vax Air Lift Steerable Pet Max corded upright
products.description: A budget corded upright from Vax and the cheapest machine in this list, a floor for anyone who just needs a vacuum that works.

economical.note: John Lewis listed it at £109.99 when checked. Scored as 100 minus one point per £10, so a £150 machine scores 85 and a £650 one 35.

longevity.note: John Lewis's listing for the Vax Air Lift Steerable Pet Max states a 2-year guarantee.

repairability.note: A corded upright, so there is no battery to wear out.

products.name: Hoover HF4 PowerMove Pets cordless (HF4P10P)
products.description: A budget cordless stick from Hoover, with a removable battery and a three-year guarantee.

economical.note: John Lewis listed it at £159.00 when checked. Scored as 100 minus one point per £10, so a £150 machine scores 85 and a £650 one 35.

longevity.note: John Lewis's listing for model HF4P10P states a 3-year guarantee.

repairability.note: John Lewis's listing names a removable battery pack among the parts in the box.

products.name: Hoover HL2 Turbo Style Pets corded upright (HL210PTG)

economical.note: John Lewis listed it at £179.99 when checked. Scored as 100 minus one point per £10, so a £150 machine scores 85 and a £650 one 35.

longevity.note: John Lewis's listing for model HL210PTG states a 2-year guarantee.

repairability.note: A corded upright, so there is no battery to wear out.

products.name: Bissell PowerClean FurGuard cordless (4091E)
products.description: A cordless stick from Bissell, aimed at pet hair. John Lewis does not say whether its battery can be swapped, so repairability is not scored.

economical.note: John Lewis listed it at £229.99 when checked. Scored as 100 minus one point per £10, so a £150 machine scores 85 and a £650 one 35.

longevity.note: John Lewis's listing for model 4091E states a 2-year guarantee.

products.name: Kärcher VC 4 Cordless myHome
products.description: A light cordless stick from Kärcher.

economical.note: Kärcher's UK shop listed it at £149.99 when checked, reduced from £199.99. Scored as 100 minus one point per £10, so a £150 machine scores 85 and a £650 one 35.

longevity.note: Kärcher UK's guarantee page gives 2 years for its home vacuum categories, or 3 years when bought directly from Kärcher UK; the table does not list cordless stick vacuums by name, so the 2-year figure is used.

products.name: Roborock Q10 S5 robot vacuum
products.description: An entry-level LiDAR robot vacuum from Roborock.

economical.note: Roborock's UK shop listed it at £129.99 when checked, on sale from a regular £249.99. Scored as 100 minus one point per £10, so a £150 machine scores 85 and a £650 one 35.

longevity.note: Roborock's UK product page states a 2-year guarantee.

privacy.note: The Q10 S5 navigates by LiDAR and is controlled through Roborock's app, which holds a map of the home. In a 2025 test of six robot vacuums against 40 security criteria, the Korea Consumer Agency found that only the Samsung and LG models met its standards across all categories; Roborock's S9 MaxV Ultra was among the Chinese-made models that fell short, and the agency said the companies concerned have since made fixes. The test covered a different Roborock model, so this is a brand-level signal.

products.name: iRobot Roomba Plus 415 Combo
products.description: A LiDAR robot vacuum and mop from iRobot, the Roomba maker, which emerged from Chapter 11 in January 2026 owned by its Shenzhen contract manufacturer, Picea.

economical.note: iRobot's UK shop listed it at £279.00 when checked, reduced from £449.00. Scored as 100 minus one point per £10, so a £150 machine scores 85 and a £650 one 35.

longevity.note: iRobot's UK product page lists a 2-Year Limited Warranty.

privacy.note: The Roomba Plus 415 maps the home with LiDAR and is run through iRobot's app. In January 2026 iRobot said its Chinese contract manufacturer Picea had acquired 100% of the company through a court-supervised Chapter 11 process, and that it had set up a separate US subsidiary, iRobot Safe, for data protection and governance. No regulator finding against Roomba data handling was found.

products.name: Ecovacs DEEBOT N20 PLUS
products.description: A budget self-emptying robot vacuum and mop from Ecovacs.

economical.note: Ecovacs's UK shop listed it at £199.00 when checked, with £229.00 shown as the higher price. Scored as 100 minus one point per £10, so a £150 machine scores 85 and a £650 one 35.

longevity.note: Ecovacs's UK product page states a 2-year guarantee, described there as a full 2-year extended warranty.

privacy.note: The DEEBOT N20 PLUS maps the home and is run through the ECOVACS HOME app. In a September 2025 assessment by Korea's Internet & Security Agency and Consumer Agency, Ecovacs was one of three Chinese brands whose app had insufficient user authentication, with flaws that could expose photos taken inside the home, and one of two whose device hardware security was rated relatively low. The assessment covered the Deebot X8 Pro Omni, a different model, so this is a brand-level signal.

products.name: eufy Omni C30 Edge robot vacuum and mop (T210QV11)
products.description: A robot vacuum and mop with an all-in-one washing and emptying station from eufy, Anker's home brand.

economical.note: John Lewis listed it at £699.00 when checked. Scored as 100 minus one point per £10, so a £150 machine scores 85 and a £650 one 35.

longevity.note: John Lewis's listing for model T210QV11 states a 2-year guarantee.

privacy.note: eufy's UK privacy policy says Anker, eufy's parent, transfers personal data within the Anker group and to third parties in other countries including China, the EEA, the UK and the US, using standard contractual clauses for UK and EEA data. No regulator finding against eufy robot vacuums was found.
